This robot hand just learned to walk on its fingertips, with no arm attached.
Engineers at ETH Zurich gave an off-the-shelf hand an 80-gram backpack: a battery, a motion sensor, and a Raspberry Pi Zero.
But a hand is built for grasping, not walking. Its fingers are different lengths, and it has a thumb.
So they trained it in simulation, with reinforcement learning: trial and error, with rewards for moving well.
Their trick is virtual springs. Each finger has a home position, and drifting away costs points.
On real hardware, it crawled across fourteen surfaces, including grass, gravel and metal grates.
When it tipped over, it righted itself in 21 of 25 tries.
The idea: robot parts that aren't stuck in one job, so a hand could detach and explore tight spaces.
